summary: 80-foot steel stairway tower in St. Louis County, Minnesota, erected by the CCC in 1934 and listed as standing; no access or staffing sources found.

facts.design: 80-foot steel stairway tower, also called Arbutus

events.note: Erected by the CCC in September 1934 at a cost of $168.30 (Register). Central lookouts give the same year and an 80-foot steel tower.
A four-post timber tower on the site was torn down in 1934 (Register).

evidence.quote: Kabetogama is an 80 foot stairway tower.

evidence.supports: Also called Arbutus; made by McClintic Marshall
evidence.quote: Also called Arbutus, it was made by the McClintic Marshall Corp of Bethleham PA.

evidence.supports: erected by the CCC in September 1934 at a cost of $168.30
evidence.quote: It was erected by the CCC in September 1934 at a cost of $168.30.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Register and Central Lookouts agree on 1934 and 80 ft (24.4 m, used in facts). No source found on access, climbing rules, staffing or condition after 2020. Two web searches and a few pages gave no access information; the Peakery page is a peak listing with no visit details, so it was not used. Register spells the maker's town 'Bethleham'; the story says Pennsylvania. Peakery lists the elevation as 1,392 ft while the Register says 1,395 ft; not in the story. Wikimedia Commons has a category of photographs (Category:Kabetogama Lookout Tower) but licences were not checked, so no photos are added. Access is left out of facts because no source supports it.
